journey.title: About Me (&) My Journey
journey.intro: I opened my first notebook for intelligent systems a few years ago. What happened after that is easier to show than explain.

spotlight.headline: Engineering Intelligent Ecosystems
spotlight.body: CSE (AIML) engineer building scalable, decentralized, and production-ready intelligent systems—from AI pipelines to high-reliability infrastructure and cloud-native deployments.

pillars.title: Systems Architecture
pillars.body: Distributed systems, consistency, and secure protocols

items.title: Starting with curiosity
items.summary: Carried forward AIML coursework and side experiments into real builds—data, models, and the systems around them.
items.detail: The early years were late nights, broken training runs, and the thrill of something that actually inferred. By 2024 that habit became systems thinking: notebooks turning into deployable services with APIs, pipelines, and interfaces people could use.

items.title: Beyond the comfort zone
items.summary: Deepfake detection, edge voice, and on-device inference pushed past “demo-ready” into real constraints.
items.detail: Shipping became the teacher. GPU inference, ensemble models, Indic ASR, and privacy-first tooling forced harder trade-offs—latency, accuracy, auth, monitoring, and what stays on-device vs in the cloud.

items.title: Systems that stay private
items.summary: Blindspot and Vaani—local AI review and offline voice UI—centered on trust and ownership of data.
items.detail: The through-line from those first experiments to now: intelligent systems people can run without surrendering their code or conversations to a black-box API. Same craft, sharper tools—the best work is still ahead.

capabilities.subtitle: Capabilities overview
capabilities.intro: The same stack from the skills map—Python and C++, models and prompts, Next.js on the surface, cloud and containers underneath—turned into systems you can actually run.

items.title: ML & GenAI Systems
items.body: Scikit-learn, TensorFlow, and Keras for classical and deep learning; LLMs, SLMs, RAG, and prompt engineering to take a model from notebook to a service.

items.title: Product Surfaces & APIs
items.body: Next.js applications wired to Python backends, Git/GitHub workflows, and clean service boundaries—integrations that hold up past the demo.

items.title: Edge & On-Device AI
items.body: Gemma, Phi-3, and other small models where data should stay local—offline-first inference when privacy and latency matter more than a cloud round-trip.

items.title: NLP & Language Pipelines
items.body: NLTK, SpaCy, and retrieval-augmented flows for summarization, extraction, and multilingual language work—not a chatbot bolted on as an afterthought.

items.title: Cloud, Data & Delivery
items.body: AWS, Azure, and GCP with Docker, CI/CD, NGINX, and VMs; PostgreSQL or MySQL when the data has to last. Deployments you can observe and hand off.

cta.title:
From models
to cloud,
let's ship it
cta.body: Python and C++ at the core, RAG and prompt engineering for the intelligence, Next.js on the surface, and AWS, Azure, or GCP with Docker and CI/CD underneath—plus PostgreSQL when the data has to last.

items.q: Do you only build research demos?
items.a: No. Demos are useful, but the focus is production-aware systems—APIs, edge constraints, observability, and handoffs your team can actually run.

items.q: Can you work with an existing codebase?
items.a: Yes. A lot of the value is auditing what you have, clarifying bottlenecks, and improving structure, performance, or model integration without a full rewrite.

items.q: What’s the process from start to launch?
items.a: It starts with goals, constraints, and success criteria. Then a clear scope, staged builds with visible progress, and a handoff you understand—not a black box dump.
Yes. Sensitive products and internal tools are treated with the same discretion as public work. Happy to sign an NDA before details.
Engineering is the core strength, with a strong product eye. If you have designers, collaboration is tight. If you have a rough direction, we can shape and bring in design help when needed.
Just reach out and describe what you have in mind. We’ll figure out a system review, a scoped build, or an iteration block from the problem—not a forced package.
